articles.articleText: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over? - Published Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment. "People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC. After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter. "Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion. Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next." Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force. Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority. Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat. "The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage." Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says. Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost. Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC. He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy." The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability. It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored. Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes. Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days. "We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active. Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents. The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds. Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded. Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC. Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations. However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael. Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF." He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says. Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says. What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded." While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours." In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict. "First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF." Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade. Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement. In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters. "If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says. Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says. Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government. However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence. In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace. "Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle. articles.title: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
articles.summary: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.

articles.titleTr: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
articles.summaryTr: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.
articles.articleText: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading? - Published Have you ever been impressed by the pictures of a property on an estate agent's website, only to find the place looks completely different when you view it in person? Then there's a chance that AI was used to enhance the images you saw. From repainted walls to imaginary lawns, estate agents are increasingly using the technology to make homes seem more appealing, arguing it helps buyers visualise the potential of a place. But experts warn it can go too far and mislead prospective buyers - a trend dubbed "housefishing". So how much AI enhancement is too much? 'The rooms were much smaller' Earlier this year Olivia Nicole, 29, was searching online for five-bedroom properties in south-west London when a house on Rightmove caught her eye. But when she arrived to view it several days later she initially thought she had come to the wrong place. "The rooms were much smaller than they were in the pictures and the decor was totally different," she tells the BBC. "Some structural features were also different." For example, there was a raised section of the wall behind the sofa that didn't appear in the images. The windows were also noticeably smaller. Olivia was so surprised she took her own pictures of the property for comparison. It later turned out the pictures she had seen on Rightmove, which also appeared on the Zoopla and Winkworth websites, were enhanced with AI. But that wasn't clear in the listing, Olivia says, and she feels the agent wasted her time. "It was frustrating, because I had taken several hours off work for the viewing which I had to make up for." All three companies told the BBC they had strict guidelines on how AI could be used on their websites and have since taken the images down. 'A surge of AI listings' Estate agents have long used wide-angle lens cameras or Photoshop to make homes seem bigger or more appealing to buyers, but AI is making this process much easier and more accessible. It is difficult to quantify how common the practice is, says the Guild of Property Professionals, a trade group of independent estate agents, but it has issued guidance on how to use AI enhancement responsibly. According to a recent survey, external of 906 UK homebuyers, one in five who had who purchased a home in the past year said they had viewed a property where the listing photos had been digitally enhanced to make the home appear better than it actually was. Jack Bushrod reviews quirky property listings he finds on Rightmove for his social media channel, Housing Horrors, and says he has seen a "surge" of AI-enhanced images over the last six months. He thinks using AI is fine up to a point - to declutter a busy room, or add furniture to an empty one so a prospective buyer can see its potential. But he draws the line at anything that misleads a prospective buyer or wastes their time. "I've seen one house where they had removed a pillar and added a window. Others might use AI to remove stains on the carpet or cracks in tiles. It's little details you would only notice in person." He says most of the enhanced images he's seen weren't clearly labelled as AI-generated. Cara, 38, is currently selling her home in Lowestoft, Suffolk, and says she was surprised when she saw the AI-enhanced pictures of her property her estate agent, Howards, put on Rightmove. In one photo, her son's room was completely emptied of toys and clutter. In another, of her daughter's room, the agent appears to have removed a doll's house, brightened the room, and used AI to change the shape of a rug, but that image has since been taken down. Cara has had several viewings so far and says that one person has commented on the differences. But she says she trusts Howards, which has acknowledged the use of AI in the property listing. "If they'd changed something structurally or it was really wild and didn't look like our home at all then I would put my foot down," she says. A spokeswoman told the BBC that Howards had now introduced a policy of labelling all AI-enhanced photos. She added that the firm never used AI "to misrepresent the fundamental features of a property". "It's about helping people imagine the possibilities, not changing the reality of what's being sold." 'Jumping on the bandwagon' Trading Standards told the BBC that estate agents can use AI to make basic enhancements to photos, or to virtually furnish an empty room or garden, as long as they indicate they have used the technology. But it says structurally changing a room, for example by adding a window, or hiding features could mislead consumers and break the law. Jack Bushrod thinks all estate agents should have to clearly label AI-enhanced photos and mention any use of the tech prominently in the key features slide of a property listing. He also expects to see more housefishing as time goes on. "My worry is the more estate agents use AI, others will see the trend and jump on the bandwagon." Additional reporting by Star McFarlane Related topics - Published18 September - Published3 November

articles.title: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
articles.summary: US lawmakers now want to question him over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.

articles.titleTr: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
articles.summaryTr: US lawmakers now want to question him over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
articles.articleText: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil - Published Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill. Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy. One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future. His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. And US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, along with other Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, publicly demanded that Huang brief Congress on the matter. If he refuses to appear voluntarily before any committee that calls him, he could be subpoenaed, one Senate staff member told the BBC. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. He is far from the first tech titan to become embroiled in revelations of infidelity. Bill Gates of Microsoft and Jeff Bezos of Amazon had affairs exposed in the last decade. Both men are now divorced from their wives. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. Because of Nvidia's size and success in recent years, such a drop can have a direct impact on the savings accounts of ordinary Americans. Nvidia's value makes up about 7% of the S&P 500 index. That index is offered as a popular index fund in US retirement savings accounts. Those account balances rise and fall with the changes of the stock market. Related topics - Published9 hours ago

articles.articleText: Maple Finance’s strategy rift sends co-founder, COO to the exits Maple Finance co-founder Joe Flanagan and COO Ryan O’Shea are leaving over disagreements about the firm’s direction as SYRUP falls despite revenue growth. Two senior executives are leaving onchain asset manager Maple Finance over disagreements about the firm’s direction as its SYRUP token slid more than 7% Thursday. Maple co-founder and executive chairman Joe Flanagan said Wednesday he would leave after seven years at the firm, describing a growing divide with fellow co-founder and CEO Sidney Powell. “Over time, our views on strategy, leadership, and life have moved further apart,” Flanagan wrote. “I believe Maple is best served by one co-founder leading it forward from here.” Chief operating officer Ryan O’Shea also said in a Thursday post on X that he would leave after nearly five years at Maple. “I’ll be stepping down as COO. I’ve come to a different view on the direction Maple should take, and I’ve decided it’s time to step aside,” he wrote. SYRUP traded at $0.12 at 10:36 p.m. UTC Thursday, down 7.5% over 24 hours and 12% over the past week, according to CoinGecko. The token had a market capitalization of about $145 million. Maple and Powell did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment by publication. Maple says leadership shakeup will not disrupt anything In a statement published Wednesday, Maple confirmed that Flanagan was stepping down as chairman and leaving the company. “This is an agreed and orderly transition,” the company said, adding that his responsibilities would move to Powell and Maple’s existing leadership team. The company did not announce a replacement chairman or specify how the departing executives’ duties would be carried out. Flanagan said his differences with Powell reached a point where they were no longer constructive. “I am choosing to leave rather than continue supporting a direction I cannot stand behind,” he said. Flanagan added that he would help with the transition through the end of 2026. O’Shea is stepping down effective Nov. 27. “I’ll have no ongoing role after that,” he wrote. The departures come as Maple looks to expand beyond crypto-backed lending. In October, Powell said the firm planned to reach more customers through fintech partnerships and lend against a wider range of assets, including payments owed on loans made by fintech companies and securities backed by assets such as mortgages. Related: Kraken, Maple launch onchain warehouse facility for crypto-backed institutional loans Revenue growth continues The announcements come as Maple’s lending business continues to grow, while SYRUP is down 62% year to date and total value locked (TVL) has declined. According to Token Terminal, Maple’s protocol revenue rose 8% year over year in October, while TVL fell around 11% between the end of September and Nov. 11. Maple’s latest quarterly results also showed growth, with the company reporting $4.4 million in third-quarter revenue, up 5% from a year earlier. Assets under management rose 18% year over year to $4.7 billion. Maple has also been using some of its revenue to buy back SYRUP tokens. In September, the company repurchased about 1.37 million tokens, twice as many as in August, according to its October update. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

articles.titleTr: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
articles.summaryTr: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
articles.articleText: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say - Published Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. As reported in the Times,, external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales. Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment. Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes. People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work. In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Speaking later on Thursday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said young people would be given support "when they need it as teenagers rather than leaving them on benefits in their 20s". He added: "The principle that we will be working on is that we will guarantee support for young people and that is the whole basis on which we will proceed." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare changes last year under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. Dame Meg Hillier, who helped spearhead a backbench rebellion against Starmer's reforms, suggested she and her colleagues were broadly supportive this time around. "What happened last year was a cut was being proposed and none of us could explain to people what would happen to them," the Labour MP told the BBC. "Milburn has done some very good work on this so I'm giving him a fair wind," she added. But Bell Ribeiro-Addy, one of the Labour backbenchers who revolted last year, said she was "not sure" she could vote to cut the benefit entitlement of existing claimants. 'Cannot assume' Tom Ashforth, a 19-year-old student at Sheffield Hallam University, receives both components of Pip at the higher rate. He said the financial support helps him manage additional expenses linked to his visual impairment, including prescriptions, mobility aids and accessible learning resources. "If I were to lose it, I would struggle to afford essential things," he said. He said he believes decisions over disability benefits should be made on a case-by-case basis, rather than according to age. "You cannot assume that everyone under the age of 25 is in the same position," he said. In his Times interview, Milburn acknowledged that changing the rules for existing claimants would be "difficult politically" but stressed it was necessary. 'Rebuilding system from scratch' James Taylor, from disability equality charity Scope, said Pip was a "lifeline" and restricting access to it "won't make young disabled people's extra costs disappear". Harriet Edwards, from the charity Sense, said changes were "long overdue", but that without additional details, families were "deeply anxious". A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work." The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. Both the Conservatives and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence. Responding on Thursday, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the government should not be spending "lots of time" on employment schemes, which she said would ultimately fail. If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch", Milburn said. His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, wherein young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. In an interview recorded on Tuesday, Skills Minister Jacqui Smith told the BBC that young people had a "responsibility" to take up employment support. "It is a contract. People need the chance, and they need to take that chance," she added. A separate review - co-chaired by disabilities minister Sir Stephen Timms - examining disability benefits is also expected to be published this month. articles.articleText: Cevdet Yılmaz'dan COP31 mesajı: "Özel sektör olmadan iklim hedeflerine ulaşılamaz" - Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi'nde 55'i aşkın ülkeden bin 500’ün üzerinde katılımcı bir araya geldi. - Zirvede iklim finansmanı, enerji güvenliği ve sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü öne çıkarken, iş dünyasının iklim hedeflerinin hayata geçirilmesindeki rolüne dikkat çekildi. Türkiye Odalar ve Borsalar Birliği (TOBB) koordinasyonunda düzenlenen COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi, 12 Kasım’da Antalya’da başladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle "Hedeften Uygulamaya" temasıyla gerçekleştirilen zirvede, iklim hedeflerinin yatırım projelerine dönüştürülmesi, enerji dönüşümü, sanayinin karbonsuzlaştırılması ve dirençli şehirler ele alındı. Zirvenin açılışında konuşan Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz, yeşil dönüşümün fosil yakıt ithalatını azaltarak makroekonomik istikrara katkı sağlayacağını belirtti. İklim hedeflerine ulaşılması için finansmana hazır projelerin ve kamu-özel sektör iş birliğinin önemini vurgulayan Yılmaz, özel sektörün sürece dahil edilmediği iklim politikalarının başarılı olamayacağını söyledi. COP31 Başkanı ve Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanı Murat Kurum ise zirveyi bir “uygulama COP’u” olarak konumlandırdıklarını ifade etti. Kurum, 2035’e kadar nihai enerji tüketiminde elektriğin payını yüzde 35’e, üretim ve imalatta döngüsel malzeme kullanımını en az yüzde 15’e çıkarma hedeflerini açıkladı. İklim Uygulama Köprüsü aracılığıyla ülkelerin önceliklerini yatırım yapılabilir projelere dönüştürmeyi amaçladıklarını belirtti. Hisarcıklıoğlu: "İklim eylemi en büyük yatırım fırsatı" TOBB Başkanı ve COP31 İş Forumu Başkanı Rifat Hisarcıklıoğlu, iklim hedeflerine müzakere salonlarında değil, fabrikalarda, tarlalarda ve şantiyelerde ulaşılabileceğini söyledi. İş dünyasının iklim eylemi açısından merkezi bir rol üstlendiğini belirten Hisarcıklıoğlu, iklim eyleminin bir maliyet değil, neslin en büyük yatırım fırsatı olduğunu vurguladı. Hisarcıklıoğlu, bu fırsatın hayata geçirilmesi için teknolojinin yanı sıra net ve istikrarlı politikalara, hızlı izin süreçlerine ve adil rekabete ihtiyaç duyulduğunu kaydetti. Dünya Bankası Başkanı'ndan özel sektör sermayesi vurgusu Zirvede düzenlenen oturumda konuşan Dünya Bankası Grubu Başkanı Ajay Banga, iklim yatırımlarının ekonomik getiriler ve genç istihdamı odağında değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini belirtti. BBVA Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Carlos Torres Vila ise gelişmekte olan ülkelerde KOBİ’lerin yeşil finansmana erişiminin önemine dikkat çekti. Vila, enerji verimliliği, elektrifikasyon, akıllı şebekeler ve yapay zekanın Türkiye gibi yüksek potansiyele sahip ülkelerin rekabet gücünü artırabileceğini ifade etti. Enerji güvenliği ve sanayinin dönüşümü gündemde Zirvenin oturumlarında enerji arz güvenliği, elektrifikasyon, iklim yatırımlarının finansmanı ve sanayinin karbonsuzlaştırılması da ele alındı. Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanı Alparslan Bayraktar, IEA İcra Direktörü Fatih Birol ve BBVA Grup CEO’su Onur Genç enerji güvenliğini değerlendirirken, Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanı Mehmet Fatih Kacır ile Sabancı Holding CEO’su Kıvanç Zaimler elektrifikasyon başlığında görüşlerini paylaştı. Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan ise şehirlerin iklim mücadelesindeki rolüne dikkat çekerek, dünya nüfusunun yarısından fazlasının şehirlerde yaşadığını ve enerjinin yüzde 70’inden fazlasının şehirlerde tüketildiğini söyledi. Khan, şehirlerin iklim krizinde ya sorunun parçası ya da çözümün kendisi olabileceğini ifade etti. COP31 İş ve Yatırım Zirvesi, 13 Kasım’da döngüsel ekonomi, KOBİ’lerin yeşil dönüşümü, iklim teknolojileri ve COP32 sürecine ilişkin oturumlarla devam edecek.

articles.titleTr: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express

articles.articleText: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express North Korean hackers launch memecoins to launder funds stolen in the Binance hack, while xStocks plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move $430,000 of stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. However, the tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain. HONG KONG Hong Kong’s wealthy investors are embracing crypto. (Chi Hung Wong) xStocks tokenizes 200 stocks in UK and EU, with hundreds from Hong Kong coming soon Kraken parent Payward’s xStocks platform has added tokenized versions of more than 200 stocks listed in the United Kingdom and European Union. Payward said the latest expansion brings xStocks’ offering to more than 1,500 tokenized assets. The company reported more than $45 billion in cumulative transaction volume and over 550,000 unique holders. Payward said it plans to add hundreds of Hong Kong-listed equities in the coming weeks. Hong Kong’s forthcoming crypto licensing regime Deputy Secretary for Financial Services Chan Ho-lim told FinTech Week the region will introduces a new licensing regime for virtual-asset trading, custody, advisory and management, via amendment bills that will be submitted to Legislative Council this year. More Hong Kong news Police have arrested 22 people in a cross border money laundering investigation, that allegedly involved a over the counter crypto network that moved more than HKD$150 million (US$18 million) while attempting to obscure the origin of funds. Meanwhile, the US has sanctioned 41 entities allegedly linked to the Cambodia’s Prince Group, including a man named Qiu Yong, who is accused of running Hong Kong companies on behalf of the criminal organization. SOUTH KOREA South Korea to permit crypto withdrawal freezes during hacking threats South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) plans to allow crypto exchanges to suspend deposits and withdrawals when hacking is suspected, rather than waiting until a breach is confirmed. The FSC said it would issue a no-action letter permitting preventive suspensions under certain conditions. Current rules prohibit exchanges from blocking withdrawals without legitimate grounds and explicitly allow restrictions only when a hacking incident is clearly established. The regulator also called for round-the-clock monitoring and incident response, higher cold-wallet holdings, and stronger insurance coverage and reserves. GOPAX puts everything on ice South Korean crypto exchange GOPAX announced on November 6 it was suspending trading, deposits and withdrawals and moving all user assets to cold wallets. The firm had received threatening emails that claimed a hack was imminent, and took the drastic step of putting everything on ice on the recommendation of financial authorities. JAPAN Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital Japanese financial services giant Nomura Holdings is reportedly weighing a sale of its cryptocurrency subsidiary Laser Digital as Nomura’s European operations continue to post losses. Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group but is yet to make a final decision and could keep the business. Nomura’s European businesses posted a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company posted pretax profits in every other reporting region over the same period. THAILAND Thailand is examining new rules for ETFs and ICO investors (Sasint) Thailand proposes $148K daily cap on stablecoin deposits and withdrawals Thailand’s securities regulator has proposed capping daily stablecoin deposits and withdrawals at 5 million baht ($148,000) each per customer at regulated crypto operators. The limit would apply separately to deposits and withdrawals at each operator, Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said in a Thursday announcement. The regulator said the rules aim to curb money laundering, cybercrime and attempts to bypass cross-border money transfer rules. The draft would bar stablecoin transfers to and from third-party wallets. More Thailand news Thailand’s SEC will block access to Bitget from December 5. It has also proposed new tests for retail investors before allowing them to invest in ICOs. The tests would require knowledge of at least six areas including digital tokens and investor rights, blockchain technology, digital-asset wallets and distribution channels. The proposals will be up for comment until November 25. The SEC is also seeking feedback on new rules around margin loans and ETFs, but has ruled out allowing leveraged or crypto ETFs at this stage. Vietnam South Korean crypto firm Bithumb Asset, has invested $85 million into a luxury resort project in Hoi An in Vietnam being built by local real estate developer Asia Estate. Da Nang police have issued a warning about scams via “ghost” cryptocurrency projects that are really just ponzi schemes in disguise. They highlighted a fraud ring involving the DRK cryptocurrency project, led by Huynh Duc Van, 33, and seven accomplices, which was recently dealt with by law enforcement. SINGAPORE Nomura’s former head of crypto derivatives trading, John Kim, has joined Chicago-based DV Trading in Singapore to lead a new discretionary crypto-trading team. A Singapore woman lost S$78,000 (US$60,391) in a four-month long crypto scam after someone posing as an insurance buyer “helped” her to set up a crypto wallet. She initially believed she was making money, before getting cleared out after she was directed to the little known Qevorinex platform. International bank communication network Swift argued at Singapore FinTech Festival for shared standards to prevent digital assets from fragmenting across incompatible systems.

articles.summary: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik askeri müdahale seçeneğini dışlamadı. Trump, 2028'de görev süresi sona ermeden önce Küba meselesini çözmek istediğini söyledi.

articles.articleText: Trump'tan Küba'ya gözdağı: "Görev sürem bitmeden halletmek istiyorum" - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik askeri müdahale seçeneğini dışlamadı. Trump, 2028'de görev süresi sona ermeden önce Küba meselesini çözmek istediğini söyledi. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Küba'ya yönelik olası bir askeri operasyon hakkında açıklamalarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Salem News Channel'a telefonla bağlanan Trump, görev süresi dolmadan önce Küba meselesini halletmek istediğini belirtti. Küba'yı "başarısız bir ülke" olarak nitelendiren Trump, ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio'nun süreci iyi yönettiğini ve gelişmeleri yakından takip ettiklerini söyledi. Küba'ya askeri güç kullanılıp kullanılmayacağına ilişkin soruyu yanıtlayan Trump, sınırlı bir operasyon seçeneğine de açık olduğunu ifade etti. Trump, "Bunun için biraz askeri güç gerekse, zayıf bir operasyon olsa bile, sizin için sorun olur mu?" sorusuna, "Benim için uygundur, bunu kesinlikle değerlendiririm." yanıtını verdi. ABD ile Küba arasındaki ilişkiler, 1959 Küba Devrimi'nden bu yana ambargo ve siyasi gerilimlerle şekilleniyor. Washington yönetimi, 1960'lardan itibaren Küba'ya yönelik ekonomik yaptırımlar uyguluyor.

articles.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
articles.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Nvidia shares plunged after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and left the board. Coinbase’s head of EU policy said tighter DeFi rules could push users toward riskier platforms. Binance’s security chief warned about fake job interviews months before attackers used a similar tactic in the exchange’s $6.3 billion hack. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and CEO and stepped down from the company’s board on Thursday, effective immediately. The board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Kress will retain her role as CFO while Nvidia’s board considers internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO role. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones its first chair and said it expects Nvidia’s operations to proceed without interruption. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Bitcoin (BTC) fell alongside Nvidia shares, dropping as much as 3.5% to a multimonth low. The shares later pared losses to trade at $165 at 4:24 p.m. UTC, down 5% on the day. The stock was down more than 26% over the previous month. EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec European Union efforts to tighten oversight of decentralized finance (DeFi) could drive crypto users toward platforms offering fewer investor protections, according to Coinbase’s head of EU policy. Roeland Van der Stappen told Cointelegraph that regulated crypto platforms could respond by limiting or dropping access to DeFi services. “Rules designed to protect investors would end up pushing activity towards the places with the least protection,” Van der Stappen said. In its September response to the European Commission’s consultation on the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), the European Securities and Markets Authority recommended creating a new category of regulated crypto services for firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols. articles.summary: FDA, Ozempic, Wegovy ve Mounjaro gibi popüler diyabet ve zayıflama ilaçlarının nadir ancak kalıcı görme kaybına yol açabilen bir göz rahatsızlığıyla ilişkili olabileceği uyarısıyla güvenlik etiketlerine yeni bilgiler eklenmesini istedi.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Zayıflama ilaçlarında kalıcı görme kaybı riski: FDA'dan yeni uyarı
articles.summaryTr: FDA, Ozempic, Wegovy ve Mounjaro gibi popüler diyabet ve zayıflama ilaçlarının nadir ancak kalıcı görme kaybına yol açabilen bir göz rahatsızlığıyla ilişkili olabileceği uyarısıyla güvenlik etiketlerine yeni bilgiler eklenmesini istedi.
articles.articleText: Zayıflama ilaçlarında kalıcı görme kaybı riski: FDA'dan yeni uyarı - FDA, Ozempic, Wegovy ve Mounjaro gibi popüler diyabet ve zayıflama ilaçlarının nadir ancak kalıcı görme kaybına yol açabilen bir göz rahatsızlığıyla ilişkili olabileceği uyarısıyla güvenlik etiketlerine yeni bilgiler eklenmesini istedi. ABD Gıda ve İlaç Dairesi (FDA), diyabet tedavisinde ve kilo verme amacıyla kullanılan bazı popüler ilaçların nadir görülen ve kalıcı görme kaybına neden olabilen bir göz hastalığıyla ilişkili olabileceği uyarısında bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kurum, GLP-1 grubu ilaçların güvenlik etiketlerine olası riske ilişkin yeni uyarılar eklenmesini zorunlu kıldı. FDA'nın açıklamasına göre, glukagon benzeri peptit-1 reseptör agonisti (GLP-1 RA) grubundaki ilaçlar, "arteritik olmayan anterior iskemik optik nöropati" (NAION) adı verilen göz rahatsızlığıyla bağlantılı olabilir. Görme sinirine giden kan akışının azalmasıyla ortaya çıkan NAION, genellikle tek gözde ani ve ağrısız görme kaybına yol açıyor. Açıklamada, mevcut tedavilerle kaybedilen görmeyi geri kazandırdığı bilinen bir yöntemin bulunmadığı belirtildi. Birçok ilacın etiketine eklenecek FDA, Novo Nordisk'in Ozempic ve Wegovy, Eli Lilly'nin Mounjaro ve Zepbound ile Sanofi'nin Soliqua ilaçları dahil olmak üzere GLP-1 etkisi gösteren tüm ilaçların güvenlik etiketlerinde olası riske yer verilmesini istedi. Diyabet ve obezite hastalarında NAION riskinin zaten yüksek olduğuna dikkat çeken kurum, söz konusu ilaçların da bu hastalıkların tedavisinde kullanıldığını hatırlattı. Novo Nordisk ise ABC News'e yaptığı açıklamada, mevcut araştırmaların GLP-1 grubu ilaçların NAION'a neden olduğunu ortaya koymadığını savundu. 100 bin kişide vaka sayısı 6,4 olarak hesaplandı FDA, GLP-1 grubu ilaçlarla NAION arasındaki olası ilişkiyi, 2024'te JAMA Ophthalmology dergisinde yayımlanan bir araştırmanın ardından incelemeye aldı. Araştırmada, Ozempic ve Wegovy'nin etken maddesi semaglutid kullanan hastalarda NAION görülme riskinin arttığına işaret edilmişti. Kurumun incelemesinde, GLP-1 grubu ilaçları kullanan her 100 bin kişi başına bir yıllık dönemde ortalama 6,4 NAION vakası tespit edildi. Başka diyabet ilaçları veya plasebo kullananlarda ise bu sayı 3,8 olarak kaydedildi. NAION, görme sinirinin kanlanmasının bozulmasıyla ortaya çıkan ve çoğunlukla tek gözde ani görme kaybına neden olan bir rahatsızlık. FDA'nın uyarısı, ilaçların bu hastalığa kesin olarak neden olduğunun kanıtlandığı anlamına gelmiyor; olası riskin güvenlik etiketlerinde belirtilmesini amaçlıyor.

articles.title: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment: Reuters
articles.summary: The prediction market operator said the decision was mutual and followed 1789 Capital’s investment in rival Polymarket, denying political considerations.

articles.titleTr: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment: Reuters
articles.summaryTr: The prediction market operator said the decision was mutual and followed 1789 Capital’s investment in rival Polymarket, denying political considerations.
articles.articleText: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket investment: Reuters The prediction market operator said the decision was mutual and followed 1789 Capital’s investment in rival Polymarket, denying political considerations. Prediction market platform Kalshi has ended its advisory relationship with Donald Trump Jr. after his venture capital firm increased its investment in rival Polymarket, Reuters reported Thursday. A Kalshi spokesperson told Reuters that talks about ending Trump Jr.’s advisory role began in August, after Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, took the lead on Polymarket’s $1 billion funding round. The round would value the company at $21 billion, with 1789 Capital set to contribute about $300 million. “We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” the spokesperson said. Trump Jr. joined Kalshi as a strategic adviser in January 2025 and received an equity stake reportedly worth $300,000 at the time, according to the Financial Times. Kalshi’s spokesperson said political considerations played no role in the decision. Two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, however, that some within Kalshi had raised concerns about what Democrats’ midterm sweep of both chambers of Congress could mean for the company. articles.title: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off
articles.summary: Strategy shares declined Thursday following MSCI’s decision to remove the company from its indexes, as Bitcoin also fell amid a broader crypto market decline.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off
articles.summaryTr: Strategy shares declined Thursday following MSCI’s decision to remove the company from its indexes, as Bitcoin also fell amid a broader crypto market decline.
articles.articleText: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off Strategy shares declined Thursday following MSCI’s decision to remove the company from its indexes, as Bitcoin also fell amid a broader crypto market decline. Shares of Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin treasury company Strategy fell 6.49% on Thursday, closing at $114.41, a day after MSCI confirmed the company’s removal from its global equity indexes and amid a broader cryptocurrency market sell-off. On Wednesday, MSCI confirmed that Strategy would be removed from its global equity indexes after the Nov. 30 market close, a move that could trigger selling by funds tracking the benchmarks. JPMorgan previously estimated that the exclusion could result in roughly $2.8 billion in selling pressure. Source: Yahoo Finance Ryan Kirkley, CEO of Global Settlement Network, told Cointelegraph that MSCI’s decision could help distinguish Bitcoin treasury companies from traditional operating businesses and limit indirect cryptocurrency exposure for passive investors. “Index inclusion meant ordinary passive investors, like someone holding a global index fund in their pension, were getting leveraged Bitcoin exposure they never chose. MSCI just fixed that,” he said. Kirkley added that MSCI’s decision also raises broader questions about whether Bitcoin treasury companies should be classified alongside traditional operating businesses. MSCI has said publicly what many people in institutional finance have been saying privately for a while: buying an asset and holding it isn’t an operating business. It’s a fund that doesn’t follow fund rules. In its Aug. 31 response to MSCI’s proposed rules, Strategy argued that the changes were a pretext for targeting digital asset treasury companies. It also downplayed the potential financial impact, saying MSCI-linked funds held approximately 13 million of its shares, representing just 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding. The stock’s decline coincided with a broader cryptocurrency market sell-off. Bitcoin traded near $71,340 as of 4:08 p.m. ET on Thursday, down 4.3% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko data. The total cryptocurrency market capitalization declined 3% to around $2.49 trillion. Magazine: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss

articles.title: SpaceX'ten iki eyalette dev yatırım: 74 milyar doları aşacak
articles.summary: Elon Musk'ın uzay şirketi SpaceX, Texas ve Arizona'da kurulması planlanan iki süper bilgisayar tesisi için 74 milyar dolardan fazla yatırım yapmayı hedefliyor. Projelerin binlerce kişiye istihdam sağlaması bekleniyor.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: SpaceX'ten iki eyalette dev yatırım: 74 milyar doları aşacak
articles.summaryTr: Elon Musk'ın uzay şirketi SpaceX, Texas ve Arizona'da kurulması planlanan iki süper bilgisayar tesisi için 74 milyar dolardan fazla yatırım yapmayı hedefliyor. Projelerin binlerce kişiye istihdam sağlaması bekleniyor.
articles.articleText: SpaceX'ten iki eyalette dev yatırım: 74 milyar doları aşacak - Elon Musk'ın uzay şirketi SpaceX, Texas ve Arizona'da kurulması planlanan iki süper bilgisayar tesisi için 74 milyar dolardan fazla yatırım yapmayı hedefliyor. - Projelerin binlerce kişiye istihdam sağlaması bekleniyor. SpaceX, ABD'nin Texas ve Arizona eyaletlerinde iki büyük süper bilgisayar tesisi kurmak için toplam 74 milyar doları aşan yatırım planını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin açıklamasına göre, Texas'ın Rio Grande Vadisi'ndeki Starbase bölgesine 24 milyar doların üzerinde, Arizona'nın Cochise County bölgesine ise yaklaşık 50 milyar dolarlık yatırım yapılacak. Texas projesi 3 binden fazla kişiye iş sağlayacak SpaceX, Starbase'de süper bilgisayar altyapısı için planlanan yatırımın inşaat aşamasında 3 binden fazla kişiye istihdam sağladığını, tesis faaliyete geçtiğinde ise 500'den fazla kalıcı iş oluşturmasının beklendiğini bildirdi. Tesisin kendi elektriğini üreteceği belirtilirken, Brownsville kentinin su ve atık su altyapısının genişletilmesi için 220 milyon dolarlık yatırım taahhüt edildi. Arizona'da 50 milyar dolarlık tesis Arizona'daki projenin inşaat aşamasında yaklaşık 5 bin 500, işletme döneminde ise 1000 kalıcı istihdam yaratması öngörülüyor. SpaceX, yerel elektrik kooperatifleriyle yürütülecek projeyle enerji altyapısının güçlendirilmesini ve elektrik faturalarının potansiyel olarak yüzde 20'ye kadar düşürülmesini hedefliyor. Tesisin kuru soğutma sistemiyle çalışacağı ve endüstriyel amaçlarla yer altı suyu kullanılmayacağı belirtildi. Starbase kentinde ayrıca doğalgazla çalışan bir elektrik santrali kurulması planlanıyor. Projeye ilişkin emlak vergisi indirimi ve ekonomik kalkınma anlaşmasının 9 Aralık'ta yapılacak Kent Komisyonu toplantısında değerlendirilmesi bekleniyor.

articles.summary: The 72-year-old is believed to have gone overboard from the Tui ship on Monday as it headed towards the Caribbean.

articles.titleTr: Search for British woman missing from Tui cruise in Atlantic called off
articles.summaryTr: The 72-year-old is believed to have gone overboard from the Tui ship on Monday as it headed towards the Caribbean.
articles.articleText: Search for British woman missing from Tui cruise in Atlantic called off - Published The search for a British woman who is believed to have gone overboard from a cruise ship while it was crossing the Atlantic has been suspended, the US Coast Guard (USCG) has said. The 72-year-old was last seen aboard Tui's Marella Voyager on Monday while the vessel was en route to the Caribbean. Staff realised she was missing on Tuesday, when they noticed her "bed untouched". USCG said the ship was approximately 500 nautical miles from the area where she was believed to entered the water when it received a missing report. It added that a coordinated international search and rescue effort had been called off on Wednesday due to factors including "the low likelihood of survival". USCG said the woman was last recorded accessing a cabin door at about midday on Monday. She is believed to have gone overboard in a remote area of the North Atlantic, roughly 1,400 nautical miles from Bermuda. In a previous statement, Tui said that after staff realised she was missing, the alarm was raised and a search carried out. The Daily Mail earlier reported that holidaymakers on board the ship had been told to abandon dinners, drinks and entertainment as the crew carried out an emergency headcount on Tuesday evening. Passengers stood in lines of four while staff scanned boarding cards to verify the identity of every person on the ship, according to the newspaper. In a statement, USCG confirmed it had received a missing report at about 19:30 EST (00:30 GMT) on Tuesday. The coast guard said staff also reported that the Marella did not have enough fuel to return to the search area. It is understood that USCG asked the ship to continue its crossing rather than reverse course and search for the woman. It said that volunteers from the coast guard then worked with search and rescue partners including the Maritime Rescue Coordination Center Delgada and the UK's Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, and issued urgent maritime broadcasts requesting assistance from ships in the area. It added that multiple commercial vessels were contacted as part of the operation to "consider search opportunities, but none were in the vicinity". Search efforts were suspended at about 15:50 EST (20:50 GMT) on Wednesday, "after considering the extensive search area, the elapsed time between the presumed incident and notification, the lack of available search assets in the remote location, negative results from maritime broadcasts, the sea state, and the low likelihood of survival", the coast guard said. The Marella Voyager, carrying around 2,000 passengers and 800 crew, left Malaga on 4 November and is due to arrive in Antigua on Friday before calling at Dominica and finishing its voyage in Barbados on Sunday. A spokeswoman for Marella Cruises earlier said it was supporting the authorities with their enquiries. It added it was "deeply saddened" by the disappearance, adding: "Our thoughts are with the guest's loved ones at this very difficult time. A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said in an earlier statement: "We are supporting the family of a British national reported missing on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean and we are in touch with the relevant authorities." In a separate case, a cruise ship pianist was found treading water on Sunday around 20 miles off the Californian coast after falling overboard. Two fishermen discovered the Royal Caribbean employee near Catalina Island and officials believe he may have been in the Pacific Ocean for nine hours, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner. articles.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul’da 12 Kasım'da 5 şirket yeni iş ilişkisi, sözleşme, yatırım, varlık satışı ve ihale gelişmelerini duyurdu. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık ve milyarlarca liralık işlemler öne çıktı.
articles.articleText: Borsa İstanbul'da 5 şirket yeni iş ilişkisi duyurdu: İşte KAP'a bildirilen sözleşme detayları Borsa İstanbul’da 12 Kasım'da 5 şirket yeni iş ilişkisi, sözleşme, yatırım, varlık satışı ve ihale gelişmelerini duyurdu. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık ve milyarlarca liralık işlemler öne çıktı. GESAN'dan 171,6 milyon TL'lik ilave sipariş Girişim Elektrik, daha önce imzaladığı reaktif güç kompanzasyon sistemleri sözleşmeleri kapsamında Başkent EDAŞ ve Toroslar EDAŞ'tan ilave sipariş aldı. Vergiler hariç siparişlerin 26,76 milyon TL'lik kısmı işçilik, 2,88 milyon dolarlık (güncel kurla 171,58 milyon TL) kısmı ise malzeme tedarikinden oluştu. Malzeme kapsamındaki ürünlerin, şirketin bağlı ortaklığı Europower Enerji tarafından üretileceği bildirildi. TCKRC 173 milyon TL'lik ihaleyi kazandı Kıraç Galvaniz, 23 Ekim 2026'da gerçekleştirilen Karayolları 4. Bölge Müdürlüğünün çelik otokorkuluk yapım ihalesinin şirket uhdesinde kaldığını açıkladı. 173 milyon TL bedelli ihaleye ilişkin kesinleşme kararı şirkete ulaştı. Nihai sözleşme sürecine ilişkin gelişmelerin kamuoyuyla paylaşılacağı bildirildi. MİA Teknoloji'den TCDD projesinde 18,3 milyon TL'lik tamamlanma MİA Teknoloji, TCDD 4. Bölge Müdürlüğü sorumluluk alanındaki demiryolu hatlarının mobil haritalama yöntemiyle envanter tespiti ve ölçümüne ilişkin projeyi tamamladı. İş artışı ve KDV dahil projenin toplam tamamlanma bedeli 18 milyon 349 bin 470,24 TL oldu. Şirket, projenin kabul işlemlerinin de sonuçlandığını bildirdi. KARÇEL'den 19,8 milyon euroluk yatırım kredisi Kardemir Çelik, Haddehane Modernizasyon Projesi kapsamında DZ Bank AG ile 19 milyon 774 bin 166 euro tutarında kredi sözleşmesi imzaladı. Çin İhracat ve Kredi Sigorta Kuruluşu Sinosure sigortası kapsamında sağlanan kredinin geri ödeme vadesi 12 yıl olarak belirlendi. Şirket, yatırımla üretim altyapısını modernize etmeyi, operasyonel verimliliği artırmayı ve üretimin çevresel etkilerini azaltmayı hedefliyor. Yatırımın orta ve uzun vadede maliyet yapısı ile kârlılığa katkı sağlaması bekleniyor. ORGE'nin hastane projesinde sözleşme büyüklüğü arttı Orge Enerji, devam eden Anatolia Antalya ve Anatolia Alanya Hastaneleri Projesi'nde sözleşme büyüklüğünün arttığını açıkladı. Buna göre, başlangıçta 589 bin 712 euro ve 46 milyon 77 bin 269 TL olan sözleşme tutarı, kesilen faturalarla 1 milyon 180 bin 885 euro ve 92 milyon 973 bin 275 TL'ye ulaştı.

articles.titleTr: US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow
articles.summaryTr: US envoy Steve Witkoff says President Putin has agreed to European negotiators joining the next round of Ukraine talks.
articles.articleText: US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow - Published US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held a fresh round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after the latest discussions aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi. The pair are now in Dublin to meet Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, and Witkoff said a new round of trilateral talks had already been agreed with Putin. But in a sign of further tension, Zelensky said on Thursday morning that Ukraine's military was again facing "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. The peace talks in the Emirates were framed as being centred around European security arrangements in a post-war scenario, although a resolution to the war sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 still appears distant. Comments by both President Vladimir Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider. Witkoff said that Europeans would join the next round of talks. "They are our partners and it's important to us that they take part," Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin in the Kremlin. Prime Minister Andy Burnham had said that UK national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join Zelensky, Witkoff and Kushner for talks in Dublin, but Downing Street later said they had been delayed, meaning the national security adviser could no longer join. Earlier on Thursday, Zelensky said Ukraine was trying to clear up the Starlink situation with the American side but added "some things" were already clear: "If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going." He did not elaborate further. Starshield was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use. Along with Starlink, it has come to play a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line. A similar issue with connectivity affected the front line in late October and lasted about a week before it was fixed and it remained unclear who had ordered the temporary restrictions. - Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap? - Published25 October Zelensky said the current disruption had been ongoing for several days and was "helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine". Meanwhile, some of the longstanding roadblocks in the peace process were addressed during the US-Russia talks in the Kremlin. The territorial issue continues to be a key point of contention, Putin said. "For us there is only one line of demarcation: the line of the state border. Because then it will be clear that we are here, and you are there. As soon as we start discussing 'grey zones'… arguments immediately start and any agreements become unstable. And there will be no lasting peace." He also suggested organising a humanitarian truce to allow for the evacuation of hundreds of civilians from a frontline area, on the model of last month's ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Putin suggested a similar five-day ceasefire for Kostyantynivka, a contested front-line Ukrainian city in the eastern region of Donetsk. Kyiv disputes that Russia fully holds the town, and a truce could help Moscow's troops to make a final push to seize it. "Considering that they brought in equipment and rotated troops in Oleshky under the guise of a humanitarian operation, it's clear what they want in Kostyantynivka," Ukrainian presidential adviser Dmitry Lytvyn told the BBC, adding that the details would need to be "clarified". But at the core of this week's talks has been the issue of European security architecture. Earlier Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said it was "clear that the current system does not work." Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin and that decisions about their continent could be made without them. Zelensky said he found the US approach of discussing a new European security order with Russia "a bit strange". "It is a significant shift in the US position that the US has now taken on board the Russian demand that the European security architecture needs to be discussed and agreed upon in parallel with the Ukraine peace talks," said the Director of the Estonian Foreign Policy Institute Kristi Raik. She said the Russians have a "long history" of wanting to revise European security architecture, intended as core principles "like sovereignty, territorial integrity, the principle that there is no use of force to some conflicts". Russia "has long looked to reduced Nato presence on the Eastern flank and that… get some kind of veto rights in decisions concerning European security and defence," Raik said. "And that's where it gets even more difficult to imagine that there could be an agreement between the Europeans and the Russians." On Thursday, Putin again repeated that the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine was "unacceptable" to Russia, and said Russia would like the Americans to engage with Europe "so that the Europeans can decide what they truly want: peace or war". During the first years of the war, Europeans cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly. That position has now shifted for many as concern that decisions about the European continent could be made without European involvement. Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations. Top EU diplomat Kaja Kallas told the BBC's Newshour programme the presence of a European official at the next meeting showed the Kremlin had "now realised that Europe is a big player here because we are the ones who have been supporting Ukraine". With financial pressures on European budgets, Kallas said it was "becoming harder to help Ukraine", but warned of the "the danger not only for the eastern flank of the European Union but actually for our whole continent" if Russian aggression was allowed to continue. The Kremlin has not confirmed the make-up of next week's talks, and at the start of the meeting, Putin had indicated he didn't want European countries to play a full role. The Russians have long cited Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle to their involvement. Speaking to Kushner and Witkoff, Putin said he was encouraging them "to work with your European allies so that they finally decide whether they want peace or war in Ukraine." Related topics - Published15 October

articles.articleText: US Justice Department, business groups and DeFi firms challenge Illinois crypto tax Industry groups argued in court filings that Illinois’ crypto tax, which applies even when a transaction yields no profit, could raise compliance costs and violate federal law. The US Department of Justice, business and financial industry groups and a coalition of decentralized finance (DeFi) firms have backed a legal challenge to Illinois’ 0.2% digital asset tax, arguing that the measure unfairly targets cryptocurrency transactions and could impose taxes even when investors make no profit. Over the past week, the Justice Department filed a statement of interest, while the US Chamber of Commerce and the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) submitted an amicus filing. A coalition that includes venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Paradigm as well as crypto protocols Uniswap and Aave Labs also filed a brief, according to a Thursday announcement from the Blockchain Association and Crypto Council for Innovation. The law, enacted in June, imposes a 0.2% tax on the value of digital assets exchanged, transferred or stored, regardless of whether a transaction generates a profit. The Digital Chamber sued Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul and state revenue official David Harris in July, followed by a separate challenge from the Blockchain Association and Crypto Council for Innovation in August. Originally scheduled to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027, the tax was delayed until July 1, 2027, allowing more time for the legal challenges. Illinois had projected the digital asset tax would generate $60 million in fiscal year 2027 revenue, according to estimates from the governor’s budget office. Illinois House Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch previously promoted the measure as part of a broader affordability agenda aimed at “closing corporate loopholes and making big tech companies and crypto billionaires pay their fair share,” the Chicago Tribune reported in July. Lawmakers involved in advancing the legislation and the governor’s office did not respond to Cointelegraph’s requests for comment before publication. Related: France advances stablecoin tax, eyes self-custodial wallets and exit tax proposals Business groups warn of crypto tax costs and legal violations In a Nov. 6 court filing, SIFMA and the US Chamber of Commerce warned that Illinois’ tax would affect banks, broker-dealers, custodians and asset managers across the country, potentially exposing them to significant compliance costs. They also highlighted the financial burden on customers. “This means that a customer who loses money owes the same tax as a customer who earns a profit,” the filing said. “And a customer who moves the same asset between two accounts faces tax (potentially on both ends) without a sale, a gain, or a change in beneficial ownership.” The groups said firms would need to develop systems to identify Illinois customers, value digital assets and determine which transactions are taxable, while facing potential criminal penalties for violations. They also argued that the tax discriminates against digital asset services because comparable transactions involving traditional assets are not taxed in the same way, potentially violating federal internet tax protections and constitutional requirements for interstate commerce and uniform taxation. DOJ challenges tax policy as DeFi firms warn of developer liability The Justice Department also weighed in on Nov. 6, saying that Illinois’ digital asset tax undermines federal efforts to promote cryptocurrency innovation and US leadership in the sector. The filing cited the creation of a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and the GENIUS Act, which established federal rules for stablecoins. The DOJ argued that less favorable tax treatment for digital assets could conflict with those policies. Separately, the DeFi coalition warned about who could be held responsible for collecting the tax. In a Nov. 11 filing, the group argued that Illinois’ proposed rules could impose obligations on software developers and other blockchain participants who lack customer information, control over user funds or the ability to collect taxes. articles.summary: ABD federal hükümetinin bütçe açığı, 2027 mali yılının ilk ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 42,1 artarak 404,1 milyar dolara ulaştı. Gelirler gerilerken harcamalardaki artış dikkat çekti.

articles.titleTr: ABD bütçesinde 2027 mali yılı hızlı başladı: Açıkta sert artış
articles.summaryTr: ABD federal hükümetinin bütçe açığı, 2027 mali yılının ilk ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 42,1 artarak 404,1 milyar dolara ulaştı. Gelirler gerilerken harcamalardaki artış dikkat çekti.
articles.articleText: ABD bütçesinde 2027 mali yılı hızlı başladı: Açıkta sert artış - ABD federal hükümetinin bütçe açığı, 2027 mali yılının ilk ayında geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 42,1 artarak 404,1 milyar dolara ulaştı. - Gelirler gerilerken harcamalardaki artış dikkat çekti. ABD federal hükümetinin bütçe açığı, 2027 mali yılının ilk ayı olan ekimde geçen yılın aynı dönemine kıyasla yüzde 42,1 yükseldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD Hazine Bakanlığı'nın yayımladığı bütçe dengesi raporuna göre açık, 404,1 milyar dolar olarak kaydedildi. Federal hükümet, 2026 mali yılının ekim ayında 284,3 milyar dolarlık bütçe açığı vermişti. Gelirler azaldı, harcamalar arttı Ekim ayında federal hükümetin gelirleri, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 8,8 azalarak 368,9 milyar dolara geriledi. Aynı dönemde harcamalar yüzde 12,2 artışla 773 milyar dolara yükseldi. ABD'nin 2027 mali yılı 1 Ekim 2026'da başladı ve 30 Eylül 2027'de sona erecek. Geçen mali yılda açık 1,99 trilyon dolara ulaşmıştı ABD federal hükümetinin bütçe açığı, 2026 mali yılında bir önceki yıla göre yüzde 12 artarak 1,99 trilyon dolara yükselmişti. Söz konusu tutar, Covid-19 salgınının etkili olduğu 2021 mali yılında kaydedilen 2,77 trilyon dolarlık açığın ardından son beş yılın en yüksek seviyesi olarak kayıtlara geçmişti. ABD'de mali yıl, her yıl 1 Ekim'de başlayıp sonraki yılın 30 Eylül'ünde sona eriyor. Federal bütçe açığı, hükümetin belirli bir dönemdeki harcamalarının gelirlerini aşmasıyla oluşuyor. Açığın büyümesi, kamu borçlanma ihtiyacını artırarak faiz giderleri üzerinde de baskı yaratabiliyor.
